document_summary: Justia mirror of N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 (2025), the New Jersey statute limiting residential security deposits to 1.5 months' rent and annual increases in additional security to 10% of the current deposit.

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Limitation (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2)
rules.requirement: An owner or lessee may not require a security deposit greater than 1.5 times one month's rent for dwelling property. Any additional security collected annually may not exceed 10 percent of the current security deposit.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; annual additional security max 10% of current deposit
rules.coverage_conditions: Real property used for dwelling purposes; applies to owners and lessees collecting security from a tenant.
rules.interaction: State-wide cap; the text does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: An owner or lessee may not require more than a sum equal to 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental according to the terms of contract, lease, or agreement as a security for the use or rental of real property used for dwelling purposes.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date is null: the document shows only the history note 'L.1971,c.223,s.4; amended 2003, c.188, s.5' and does not state when the requirement or the 10% provision took effect. Secondary source (Justia mirror); disclaimer says the text may not be the most recent version.
